C0.quote: We study diversity in approval-based committee elections

C1.quote: requires Ω(m2 ) non-adaptive queries, where m is the number of candidates
C1.note: Main results are query-complexity bounds and approximation algorithms. Experiments use Polis data and synthetic data.

C2.1.value: approval profile; approval sets; approval ballots; votes; query responses
C2.1.quote: The sequence of sets A = (A(1), . . . , A(n)) is called the approval profile

C2.2.quote: every voter vi ∈ V approves of a subset of the candidates

C2.3.quote: the voters are inaccurate in reporting their true approvals
C2.3.note: The introduction also refers to voters' true beliefs and opinions.

C2.4.quote: a p-inaccurate query as Ap (i, j) := A(i, j) ⊕ X
C2.4.note: True approvals A and reported answers Ap have separate notation in the inaccurate setting.

C3.1.quote: we assume each query A(i, j) is incorrect with a probability p
C3.1.note: Deviations are random noise, not strategic choices.

C3.2.quote: for accurate information, we write A(i, j) to query the opinion
C3.2.note: In the accurate and incomplete settings a query returns the voter's true approval.

C3.3.quote: which equals 1 in case voter vi approves candidate cj
C3.3.note: No reason is given for accurate answers.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction notion is used for voters in the model. 'Unsatisfiable' appears only once, in preprocessing.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: score of W equals the number of voters that have a representative
C5.1.note: Chamberlin-Courant score measures representation of voters.

C5.2.quote: voters are inaccurate in reporting their true approvals
C5.2.note: The score is computed on the true approvals A, not on the noisy reports Ap. In the accurate setting the two coincide.

VOT.quote_behav: we assume each query A(i, j) is incorrect with a probability p
VOT.note: Voters answer queries truthfully or with random noise.
